bluf: TRKKN, formerly Trakken, is a German enterprise analytics firm and Google Marketing Platform and Google Cloud partner and reseller, listing 33 office locations, that implements and resells Google's measurement stack and adds conversion optimization, cloud engineering and GenAI use cases. It is publishing steadily, with 21 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and insights through 2026-09-25, and it hosts the Analytics Summit. The Horus read puts it at 48.2, Tailwind band, percentile 99. A rival should know its analytics core is well defended; the soft ground is CRO, contradicted on its own site, and AI search, which it does not sell.
doing:
The positioning line, a Google Marketing Platform and Google Cloud partner and reseller delivering digital analytics, conversion optimisation, ad tech, AI, cloud engineering and data strategy, decodes as a Google stack integrator: it implements Google's analytics, advertising and cloud tools for large companies and, through a Licensing line for Google platform reselling, also sells the licenses themselves. The headline claim, that it hosts the Analytics Summit, billed as Europe's biggest Google Analytics event, is quoted as a claim.

The sold mix leads with Data & Measurement at 3: the title and H1 lead with analytics, and the capability note cites GA360 checkout and BigQuery Google Ads intelligence cases. CRO scores 2 as its other core line, on a Conversion Optimization service and an Optimize 360 testing case for an international fashion retailer. AI Automation / Agents and Programmatic & CTV score 1 and everything else 0, for a breadth of 4. The two partners are its Google Marketing Platform partner and reseller status and a Google Cloud partnership; the record lists no proprietary product.

The AI posture is enterprise implementation, not visibility: it pitches production ready GenAI use cases and an Advanced Analytics & AI line, and publishes on turning ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot into business value. Moves: an undated rebrand from Trakken to TRKKN, with trakken.de redirecting; the Analytics Summit 2026, pitched on server side tracking, privacy compliance and GenAI use cases; and an insights run from 2026-08-05 to 2026-09-25 on AI ready Google Ads tracking, Google Tag Manager changes and server side GTM. The record shows no pricing, no open jobs and no named owner. Conspicuously absent for a firm of its reach: SEO, paid search and paid social all score 0, with programmatic at 1, so it feeds media it does not run.
clients:
The ICP is enterprise, and the record lists three verticals: fashion retail, manufacturing and utilities. The home market is Germany, with 33 office locations listed across the Americas, EMEA and Asia Pacific.

The needs read holds no named clients, so none is names only and none is shared with another tracked agency. The eight case pages all carry the title TRKKN! and a lastmod of 2024-03-25, and their excerpts are page code rather than text, so the read had nothing to code. The capability notes describe three cases without naming the client: a GA360 checkout case and a BigQuery Google Ads intelligence case, both data and measurement needs, and an Optimize 360 testing case for an international fashion retailer, a conversion need the taxonomy files under web build and platform (inferred).

The insights feed names two brands the needs read misses. Puma appears in a case study slug dated 2026-08-12 on bigger orders and lower costs from first party data activation via value based bidding, which reads as paid performance built on data and measurement. Volkswagen appears in a 2026-09-18 success story with PHD, featured on Think with Google, with the work not described. A further case slug, dated 2026-08-06, credits 74 percent less developer involvement with enhanced tagging for an unnamed client.

What the base needs next: under KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) and KJ9 (measurement gets worse before it gets better), these enterprise accounts very likely keep buying first party data, tagging and measurement rebuilds, the work it already sells (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do: 0 of 1 tested lines practised. CRO is contradicted: it sells conversion optimization and no testing tool is detected on its own homepage, the one gap the Radar lists. The tag scan finds only OneTrust, with no gtm or ga4, which for a Google Analytics specialist more likely reflects consent gated or server side loading, a practice its insights sell, than an absent stack (moderate confidence). The Transparency Center lookup was blocked, so the record holds no Google ad count, and the LinkedIn Ad Library name query returns 0 ads. No social pixels or ABM stack show, and its LinkedIn and Instagram handles still read trakken.
market:
The Horus read scores TRKKN 48.2 on the tailwind index, Tailwind band, percentile 99. It is best placed for KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer (net 0.875, driven by Data & Measurement with AI Automation / Agents), and KJ9, measurement gets worse before it gets better (net 0.75). Its only listed headwind is slight: KJ5, the price of attention splits in two (net -0.096, Programmatic & CTV). Best fit is The Walled Oasis at 43/100. It makes none of the P moves: absent on P1, P2, P6 and P7, unknown on P5, with P3, P4 and P8 not applicable.

The Monsoon read is 47.7, band Breeze, percentile 22, with migration 53.7 above displacement 41.7. The verdict puts 42 of it in the sold mix, Data & Measurement (20) and CRO (14) carrying the most movable hours. The footprint is observed: hub offices in Bengaluru, Bogota, Prague and Santiago, plus a white label term, and the shore split sends 48% of movable work to Eastern Europe and 34% to South and Southeast Asia. It makes no onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest opening is CRO. Its own homepage contradicts the line, the one CRO case in the record is an Optimize 360 testing case for an international fashion retailer on a page last modified 2024-03-25, and the case excerpts are unreadable. A rival with a live experimentation program and dated results is likely, moderate confidence, to win testing budgets in its fashion retail accounts, since owning the analytics does not guarantee the testing work. Falsifier: a testing tool detected on trkkn.com, or a CRO case dated after 2024-03-25, at the next compile.

AI search is the second opening: P1 is absent and AI Search / GEO scores 0 while it publishes on ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot, so AI visibility for its enterprise accounts is unclaimed by it, and a rival selling that line meets no incumbent product.

The core is not an opening. With KJ4 and KJ9 as tailwinds at percentile 99, a head on attack on its analytics work is unlikely to succeed, and the KJ5 exposure is too slight to matter. With no public pricing and a Licensing line that resells Google platforms, a platform neutral measurement pitch has a roughly even chance, low confidence.
watch: Indicator I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, next reading December 2026 to January 2027: any disclosed AI checkout GMV would feed KJ4, its strongest tailwind, while high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

Indicator I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would test a firm that publishes no pricing and resells Google licenses.

Follow up the Analytics Summit 2026, pitched on server side tracking, privacy compliance and GenAI use cases: a dated agenda naming client speakers would add named clients to a record that holds none.
Follow up the insights feed, last dated 2026-09-25, for further named case studies like the 2026-08-12 Puma slug, which would move the needs read off zero.
Follow up the rebrand: LinkedIn and Instagram still read trakken, and an ownership disclosure or a completed handle change would settle the status note's judgment call.

The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile, and an unblocked Transparency Center lookup would add its first Google ad count.
